title: OpenAI Reportedly Explores Legal Options Against Apple Over AI Partnership
author: Sarah Jenkins
excerpt: Reports say tensions between Apple and OpenAI have escalated as Apple expands AI partnerships beyond ChatGPT, prompting OpenAI to reportedly explore legal options.

title: Waymo Driverless Cars Become Trapped in Atlanta Suburb After Glitch
author: Alex Thorne
excerpt: A software glitch caused multiple Waymo driverless cars to repeatedly circle and become trapped in an Atlanta suburb, raising new concerns about autonomous vehicle safety and reliability.

title: SpaceX Successfully Launches Starship V3 in Major Milestone for Mars Program
author: Emily Rodriguez
excerpt: SpaceX launched its upgraded Starship V3 rocket on a major test flight, marking a significant milestone for Elon Musk’s Mars ambitions and the future of reusable space travel.

title: Intel Launches Arc G3 Chips for Handheld Gaming PCs
author: Jessica Wu
excerpt: Intel unveiled its new Arc G3 processor family designed for handheld gaming PCs, aiming to compete with AMD-powered portable gaming devices.

title: Google Chrome Criticized Over Hidden Gemini Nano AI Downloads
author: Alex Thorne
excerpt: Google Chrome faces criticism after reports revealed the browser quietly downloads large Gemini Nano AI files onto devices, raising major privacy and storage concerns.

title: Hypershell Launches AI-Powered Exoskeletons Designed for Mainstream Consumers
author: Emily Rodriguez
excerpt: Hypershell unveiled its new AI-powered exoskeleton lineup featuring lightweight wearable robotics designed to assist hiking, running, and outdoor performance activities.

title: Hackers Use Fake GTA VI Downloads to Spread Dangerous Malware and Phishing Scams
author: Cybersecurity Desk
excerpt: Cybersecurity researchers warned that scammers are exploiting excitement around Grand Theft Auto VI with fake beta tests, phishing pages, malware downloads, and fraudulent pre-orders.

title: Apple and Google Launch Encrypted RCS Messaging for iPhone and Android
author: Robert Miller
excerpt: Apple and Google have started rolling out end-to-end encrypted RCS messaging, bringing stronger privacy and secure texting between iPhone and Android users.
